questions.question: Inside a seed, which part is the tiny baby plant?
questions.options: The cotyledon | The embryo | The stigma | The seed coat
questions.explanation: The embryo is the tiny baby plant waiting inside the seed. The cotyledon is its packed lunch, and the seed coat is its jacket.

questions.question: Which set of three things does a seed need in order to germinate?
questions.options: Water, light and sugar | Soil, wind and light | Light, salt and warmth | Water, warmth and air
questions.explanation: A seed wakes up when it has water, warmth and air. It does not need light until the young shoot pushes above the soil.

questions.question: Layla puts one bean seed in a warm cupboard and an identical bean seed in a cold fridge. Both get the same water and the same air. What is she testing?
questions.options: Whether soil is needed for germination | Whether beans taste better warm | Whether light changes how well a seed germinates | Whether temperature changes how well a seed germinates
questions.correctAnswer: Whether temperature changes how well a seed germinates
questions.explanation: Only the temperature is different, so temperature is the thing being tested. Keeping everything else the same makes it a fair test.

questions.question: A farmer plants his maize seeds far apart instead of all in one crowded patch. Why does this help the plants?
questions.options: Each plant gets enough light, water and space to grow well | The seeds germinate without any water | Crowded plants cannot make seeds at all | The plants can walk to find food
questions.correctAnswer: Each plant gets enough light, water and space to grow well
questions.explanation: Plants growing too close together compete for light, water and nutrients, so spacing them out gives every plant a fair share.

questions.question: Which part of a flower makes the pollen?
questions.options: The sepal | The stigma | The root | The anther
questions.explanation: The anther sits on top of the stalk-like filament and holds the dusty pollen. The stigma is the sticky part that catches pollen.

questions.question: What happens during pollination?
questions.options: A seed grows into a young plant | Roots take in water from the soil | Pollen travels from an anther to a stigma | Petals drop off in the wind
questions.correctAnswer: Pollen travels from an anther to a stigma
questions.explanation: Pollination is the pollen journey from anther to stigma. Bees, birds and the wind are all good pollen taxis.

questions.question: A coconut floats across the sea and grows on a new beach far away. This is an example of:
questions.options: Germination in the dark | Melting | Seed dispersal by water | Pollination by insects
questions.explanation: Plants cannot walk, so their seeds travel. A floating coconut is dispersal by water, which stops the new plant crowding its parent.

questions.question: Which state of matter keeps both its own shape and its own volume?
questions.options: A solid | Water vapour | A liquid | A gas
questions.explanation: A solid holds its shape because its particles are packed tightly in place. A liquid keeps its volume but takes the shape of its container.

questions.question: A dish of water is left on a sunny windowsill. After three days the dish is empty. What has happened to the water?
questions.options: It has frozen into ice | It has evaporated into the air | It has disappeared for ever | It has turned into a solid on the dish
questions.correctAnswer: It has evaporated into the air
questions.explanation: Warmth gives the water particles enough energy to escape as an invisible gas called water vapour. The water is still there, just spread out in the air.

questions.question: Which change happens when heat is taken away from a gas such as water vapour?
questions.options: Condensation | Evaporation | Dissolving | Melting
questions.explanation: Cooling a gas makes it condense back into a liquid. That is why water drops appear on a cold window on a chilly morning.

questions.question: Sara wants to find out whether moving air makes water evaporate faster. She puts water in two identical dishes in the same warm room and points a fan at one dish. What must she keep the same in both dishes?
questions.options: The number of dishes near the window | The amount of water she starts with | The colour of the fan | The speed of the fan
questions.correctAnswer: The amount of water she starts with
questions.explanation: In a fair test only one thing changes — here, the moving air. Everything else, including the starting amount of water, must stay the same.

questions.question: Which of these is a light source?
questions.options: A candle flame | A white wall | The Moon | A mirror
questions.explanation: A light source makes its own light. Mirrors, the Moon and pale walls only bounce back light that came from somewhere else.

questions.question: Why can you see a book lying on a table?
questions.options: The book lets all the light pass through it | Your eyes send out beams of light onto the book | Light bounces off the book and travels into your eyes | The book makes its own light
questions.correctAnswer: Light bounces off the book and travels into your eyes
questions.explanation: We see objects that are not light sources because light reflects off them and enters our eyes. Eyes receive light; they do not send it out.

questions.question: A material you can see through clearly, like clean window glass, is described as:
questions.options: Transparent | Translucent | Magnetic | Opaque
questions.explanation: Transparent materials let nearly all the light through. Translucent ones let some light through but blur it, and opaque ones block it.

questions.question: How is a shadow made?
questions.options: Light passes straight through clear glass | An opaque object blocks light travelling in straight lines | A mirror sends light back to its source | The air cools down at night
questions.correctAnswer: An opaque object blocks light travelling in straight lines
questions.explanation: Light travels in straight lines, so when something opaque gets in the way it leaves a dark patch behind it — that patch is the shadow.

questions.question: You shine a torch at a toy to make a shadow on the wall. What happens to the shadow when you move the torch closer to the toy?
questions.options: The shadow gets bigger | The shadow turns into a light source | The shadow changes colour | The shadow gets smaller
questions.explanation: Moving the light closer means the toy blocks more of the spreading light, so the shadow grows. Moving the torch away shrinks it again.

questions.question: The shadow of a stick in a playground moves and changes length during the day. Why?
questions.options: Shadows give out their own light | The ground pushes the shadow along | The Sun appears to move across the sky as the Earth spins | The stick slowly grows taller
questions.correctAnswer: The Sun appears to move across the sky as the Earth spins
questions.explanation: The Earth turns, so sunlight arrives from a changing direction. That is how shadow clocks and sundials tell the time.

questions.question: What is at the centre of our Solar System?
questions.options: Mars | The Moon | The Earth | The Sun
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star at the centre, and all eight planets, including our Earth, orbit around it.

questions.question: Why do we have day and night?
questions.options: The Sun switches itself off each evening | The Earth stops moving at night | The Moon covers the Sun every night | The Earth spins once on its axis every 24 hours
questions.correctAnswer: The Earth spins once on its axis every 24 hours
questions.explanation: As the Earth spins, the side facing the Sun has day and the side facing away has night. The Sun never switches off.

questions.question: About how long does the Moon take to go through all of its phases, from one full Moon to the next?
questions.options: About 28 days | About 365 days | About 24 hours | About 7 days
questions.explanation: The Moon takes roughly 28 days — about a month — to move through its whole cycle of phases.

questions.question: An animal that has a backbone is called a:
questions.options: Producer | Invertebrate | Mineral | Vertebrate
questions.explanation: Fish, birds, reptiles, amphibians and mammals all have backbones, so they are vertebrates. Insects and worms have none, so they are invertebrates.

questions.question: In the food chain grass → goat → lion, which living thing is the producer?
questions.options: All three | The grass | The lion | The goat
questions.explanation: Producers make their own food using sunlight, and green plants such as grass do exactly that. The goat and the lion are consumers.

questions.question: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
questions.options: Coal | Petrol | Oil | Sunlight
questions.explanation: Renewable sources such as sunlight, wind and moving water do not run out. Coal, oil and petrol come from underground stores that cannot be replaced.

questions.question: Which of these stores energy that we can use later?
questions.options: A mirror | A shadow | An echo | A battery
questions.explanation: A battery keeps energy stored inside until a circuit lets it flow. Shadows, echoes and mirrors do not store energy at all.

questions.question: What is the change from a liquid into a gas called?
questions.options: Evaporation | Condensation | Melting | Freezing
questions.explanation: Heating a liquid enough turns it into a gas, and that change is called evaporation. Cooling a gas back to a liquid is condensation.

questions.question: The thin, solid outer layer of the Earth, where we live, is called the:
questions.options: Crust | Crater | Mantle | Core
questions.explanation: The crust is the rocky skin on the outside of the Earth. Below it lie the hot mantle and, deepest of all, the core.

questions.question: At what time of day is your shadow usually longest?
questions.options: Only when you stand still | Early morning and late afternoon, when the Sun is low | Only when the sky is cloudy | At midday, when the Sun is high overhead
questions.correctAnswer: Early morning and late afternoon, when the Sun is low
questions.explanation: A low Sun sends light in at a slant, which stretches your shadow out long. When the Sun is high overhead your shadow is short.

questions.question: What does a switch do in an electrical circuit?
questions.options: It stores electricity for later | It makes the wires longer | It closes the circuit to let electricity flow, or opens it to stop the flow | It changes the colour of the bulb
questions.correctAnswer: It closes the circuit to let electricity flow, or opens it to stop the flow
questions.explanation: A switch is a gap you can open and close. Closed, the circuit is complete and the bulb lights; open, the flow stops.

questions.question: Which of these is a living thing?
questions.options: A rock | A mango tree | A metal key | A plastic spoon
questions.explanation: Living things grow, need water and food, and can make new living things. A mango tree does all of that; rocks and spoons do not.

questions.question: You open a drawer by moving it towards you. Which force are you using?
questions.options: Floating | Melting | A pull | A push
questions.explanation: Moving something towards you is a pull; moving it away from you is a push. Both are forces.

questions.question: Which of these makes its own light?
questions.options: The Sun | A mirror | A window | A book
questions.explanation: The Sun is our biggest natural light source. Mirrors, books and windows only pass on or bounce back light that came from somewhere else.

questions.question: Which of these needs electricity to work?
questions.options: A pencil | A wooden spoon | A torch | A paper kite
questions.explanation: A torch needs a battery to make its bulb light up. Pencils, kites and wooden spoons work with no electricity at all.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood all around your body?
questions.options: The brain | The heart | The stomach | The lungs
questions.explanation: The heart is a strong muscle that pumps blood through your body day and night. The lungs take in air and the stomach breaks down food.

questions.question: Which object would a magnet attract?
questions.options: A rubber band | A plastic straw | A wooden block | An iron nail
questions.explanation: Magnets attract magnetic metals such as iron and steel. Plastic, wood and rubber are not magnetic, so nothing happens.
